purpose: First cross-system progression spine for MathBridge. It aligns broad mathematical development without pretending that same-numbered grades are equivalent curricula.

CN.label: China
CN.granularity: National standard uses 1-2, 3-4 and 5-6 learning stages; exact grade sequencing comes from current approved textbook evidence.

UK.label: England
UK.granularity: Statutory year-by-year programmes of study for Years 1-6.

US.label: US — Common Core baseline
US.granularity: Grade-specific standards; not universal across all US states.

sequence.placement: Grade 1 upper — current PEP 12th series, partial verified
sequence.focus: Two consecutive early-number units: 5以内数的认识和加、减法 followed by 6～10的认识和加、减法; number meaning, composition/decomposition and operations are developed together.
Develop meaning of whole numbers up to 10,000, positional value, comparison, and connections among quantities, representations and numerals.
Extend whole-number structure beyond 10,000 and deepen understanding of the decimal/base-ten system and calculation structures.
Use the structure of counting units to connect whole numbers, decimals, fractions and operations; exact current textbook semester placement remains edition-specific.
Count/read/write to 100; begin place value beyond 20.
Two-digit tens/ones; compare/order to at least 100.
Three-digit hundreds/tens/ones; compare/order to 1,000.
Four-digit place value; numbers beyond 1,000; rounding and negative-number introduction.
Whole numbers to at least 1,000,000 plus deeper decimal place value.
Whole numbers to 10,000,000; rounding and negative numbers in context.
Tens and ones; numbers to at least 100.
Base-ten notation to 1,000; hundreds/tens/ones.
Use place value for rounding and multi-digit arithmetic.
Generalise place value; each place is ten times the place to its right; multi-digit comparison and rounding.
Extend base-ten structure to decimal thousandths and powers of ten.
No standalone NBT strand; extend number understanding to rational and negative numbers.

comparison_notes: Do not compare only by grade number: China’s national source is stage-based while England and Common Core provide finer year/grade granularity.
A useful teacher-facing comparison is not simply 'who teaches larger numbers earlier' but how each system uses representations, counting units and place-value structure to support later operations.

progression_strands.name_cn: 乘法思维 → 基本事实流利度 → 笔算方法

CN.focus: National learning-stage requirements are combined with current PEP evidence that related multiplication units were reorganised/merged. Exact full Grade 1-6 PEP unit sequence remains under direct volume verification.

sequence.focus: Concrete/pictorial multiplication and division problems; arrays, grouping and sharing foundations.
2, 5 and 10 tables; arrays, repeated addition, grouping/sharing, commutativity and inverse relations.
Build table fluency, reaching 12×12 by end of Year 4, while developing written and mental methods.
Apply facts and properties to larger numbers, factors/multiples, multi-digit multiplication and division, and increasingly complex problem solving.
Equal groups and arrays as foundations for multiplication.
Formal meaning of products/quotients, properties/inverse relationships, fluency within 100.
Multi-digit multiplication/division using place value, properties, arrays and area models.
Fluent multi-digit multiplication and division plus decimal operations.
Fluent multi-digit/decimal computation and extension of division to fraction-by-fraction division.

progression_strands.name_en: Equal Shares → Fractions as Numbers → Equivalence → Operations
progression_strands.name_cn: 等分 → 分数作为数 → 等值关系 → 分数运算

CN.focus: Use national-stage expectations plus the current PEP '计数单位' structural thread. Exact grade/semester mapping must be filled only from verified current PEP volumes.

sequence.focus: Halves and quarters of objects, shapes and quantities.
Thirds/quarters/halves/three-quarters, simple equivalence and fraction counting.
Fractions as numbers on a number line, simple equivalence/comparison and same-denominator addition/subtraction.
Equivalent-fraction families, hundredths, fractions-decimals connections and deeper same-denominator work.
Improper/mixed fractions, related-denominator addition/subtraction, fraction × whole number, fraction-decimal-percentage links.
Unlike-denominator addition/subtraction, fraction multiplication, division of proper fractions by whole numbers and equivalence across fractions/decimals/percentages.
Equal-share foundations are embedded largely in geometry rather than a formal fractions domain.
Formal fractions-as-numbers domain; unit fractions, number line, equivalence and comparison.
Explain equivalence with visual models, compare unlike fractions, build fractions from unit fractions and multiply a fraction by a whole number.
Unlike-denominator addition/subtraction, fraction-as-division, fraction multiplication and limited fraction division.
Full extension to division of fractions by fractions.

comparison_notes: The most useful classroom comparison is the meaning attached to fractions and the representations used before procedures, not merely the first year in which the word 'fraction' appears.

US Common Core makes a particularly explicit shift in Grade 3 to fractions as numbers on a number line; England introduces fraction language earlier and develops number-line/equivalence connections progressively.

publication_rules: Never convert a Chinese 1-2 learning-stage statement into an exact Grade 1 or Grade 2 claim without current textbook evidence.
UK mode must be labelled England where statutory curriculum claims are made.
US mode must identify Common Core as the baseline and allow state-specific overlays.
Teacher-facing text should paraphrase source requirements; exact quotations/source locators remain internal evidence metadata.
